#Web API of Wren (Wasm imports)

On this page

  • The Odin SDK
  • ABI
  • Modules

Every function a page or worker module can import, generated from api/*.widl. The same description produces the host trampolines (src/page/api_generated.odin), the Odin guest SDK (sdk/odin), these pages and the conformance tests (examples/apiconformance, src/tools/apiconformance).

#The Odin SDK

sdk/odin is a collection of packages, one per area of the API: a module, or the modules of one package below. A program names the collection when it is built and imports the packages it uses:

Odin
import "wren:core"   // errors, host objects, promises, buffers, events: what every other package uses
import "wren:dom"
odin build . -target:freestanding_wasm32 -no-entry-point -default-to-nil-allocator -collection:wren=<path to sdk/odin>
  • wren:core holds the modules web, async, events.
  • wren:webcodecs holds the modules webcodecs, webcodecs_audio_decoder, webcodecs_codec, webcodecs_encoders, webcodecs_image, webcodecs_video_decoder.
  • any other module is the package of its name (module dom is wren:dom).

Names are the Web IDL names of this description, without an interface prefix that repeats the package's name: Fetch_promise of module fetch is fetch.promise, console_log is console.log, URL_parse is url.parse (the prefix compared without case); a prefix naming one interface among several of the package stays (dom.Node_appendChild, dom.Document_getElementById), and so does one whose rest would be an Odin keyword or a builtin the wrappers call. A function's page says its Odin name when it differs.

#ABI

IDL typewasm parametershost implementation receivesOdin guest
i32 u32 i64 u64 f32 f64the same valuethe samethe same
booli32 (0 = false)boolbool
stringaddress, length (bytes)string, valid UTF-8 (else an error)string
usvstringaddress, lengthstring, invalid sequences replaced by U+FFFDstring
bytesaddress, length[]u8[]u8
out bytesaddress, capacity[]u8 to fill[]u8
optional string / bytesaddress, length = all ones when absentMaybe(...)Maybe(...)
T[] (numbers, handles)address, element count[]T (handles: []u64)[]T
handle (Node, URL, ...)i64 (0 = null)Api_<Handle>%!(MISSING ARGUMENT)%!(MISSING CLOSE BRACE)andle, data} when the API checks it, else u64distinct u64
enum / flagsi32 or u32Api_<Enum> / bit_set (out of range = an error)enum / bit_set
structone wasm value per field, in orderApi_<Struct>struct
callbacki32: index in the module's function tableu32procedure value

Addresses and lengths are i32 for a module whose memory 0 is 32-bit and i64 for a memory64 module: the browser defines each import with the width of the importing module's memory 0, which is the memory every pointer refers to (other memories of a multi-memory module are not visible to the browser).

Results:

  • a number, bool, enum or handle is the wasm result;
  • a string (or bytes) result takes two more parameters, a buffer (address, capacity) the browser fills with what fits; the wasm result (address-sized) is the full length, so a guest can retry with a bigger buffer;
  • a function that raises returns an i32 status: 0, or a negative Error; its result, if any, is written to a return pointer (the last parameter; a string result keeps the buffer convention, a negative length being the error); the message of the last error is Exception_message (module web);
  • a struct result is always written to a return pointer (C layout, natural alignment).

A pointer outside the memory is a trap (as an out-of-bounds load would be). An argument the browser cannot accept (invalid UTF-8 in a string, a handle that is not live or of another kind, an enum out of range) is an error for a function that raises (Type, Invalid_Handle, Invalid_Argument) and a trap for one that does not.

Availability: Window = page modules, Worker = dedicated worker modules; a worker module that imports a function not exposed to workers is not instantiated.
